---BEGIN DRAFT (to be sent to Procurement)---
Subject: Redwood cost assumptions for MAP close — Acme Health (ACME-6781)

Overview:
Redwood Inference confirms the following baseline cost and runtime assumptions for the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) associated with Acme Health. These assumptions reflect the model variant and runtime configuration outlined in the MAP and are intended to support procurement sign-off and SOW finalization.

1) Tokens per dollar (examples)
- Baseline model (redwood-open-8k, int8 quantized): ~1,200,000 input+output tokens per $1 at our hosted list price when continuously batched under the usage profile provided.
- High-throughput configuration (dedicated + aggressive batching, 1k sustained qps): ~2,200,000 tokens per $1 due to improved GPU packing and reduced overhead.
- Conservatively shielded mode (privacy routes with no prefetch, lower batch sizes): ~550,000 tokens per $1.

2) Caching behavior
- Prefix caching: supported for deterministic prompt prefixes; TTL default 24 hours, configurable per-route. Cached hits bypass full model inference and are priced at a reduced fetch rate (applies to repeated prompts/KB lookups).
- KV cache for chat sessions: session history is paginated into KV cache for reuse; cache hit rates depend on average session length and prompt reuse patterns.

3) Batching & prefetch
- Default: continuous asynchronous batching tuned for 99ms median latency with dynamic batch windows.
- Prefetch: optional, best-effort prefetching for predictable completion workflows (e.g., autocomplete or candidate reranking). Prefetch increases token throughput efficiency but requires explicit enablement for privacy-sensitive routes.

4) SLA & pricing impact
- Guaranteed 1k qps sustained requires Dedicated capacity reservation; this changes billing to a committed monthly price (we provided a separate Dedicated quote).
- For hosted mode with burst capacity, costs are usage-based and subject to transient latency variance; tokens/$ above assume the recommended defaultdict batching + caching.

5) Safety margin & acceptance
- We recommend a 15% cost buffer in the MAP for initial production ramp to account for prompt drift and lower-than-expected cache hit rates.

Attachments referenced: Acme Q2 usage profile (used to derive baseline).

---END DRAFT---

Rohan — please confirm the numeric token/$ samples and whether the TTL/buffer numbers need adjustment. Once we have confirmation, Sean can send to procurement (Sara) for sign-off.

Marissa/Sean/Sara —

Verified the draft; a couple of quick clarifications to keep it defensible for procurement:
- Tokens/$ figures: the numbers are realistic if Acme uses the quantized variant we discussed. I'll add a short parenthetical note in the final doc: "examples based on int8 quantization and 8k context; actual rate varies by model and prompt entropy."
- Cache TTL: default 24 hours is OK; suggest we call out that customers can set per-route TTL from 1h–30d and that long TTLs increase the risk of stale responses for dynamic content.
- Prefetch & privacy: we'll explicitly call out "prefetch disabled by default for any route flagged as PHI" to satisfy Acme's governance team.
- 1k qps: to guarantee <100ms p95 at 1k sustained you'll need dedicated reserved capacity — I'll attach a short note describing expected latency bands for hosted vs dedicated.

I'll add the parenthetical clarifications and the latency bands and send a final one-pager in the next hour.
